blocks.title: Chromatogram and locating agent
blocks.text: Once the paper is dried, the pattern on it is the chromatogram. Coloured components can be identified visually; if they are colourless the chromatogram must be developed by chemical or physical techniques. A locating agent is a chemical that reacts with colourless substances, such as amino acids, to give coloured products visible for inspection.
A convenient way to visualise a colourless chromatogram is to view it under a UV lamp, where the spots appear coloured. Alternatively a locating agent such as ninhydrin is used to locate the spots.
